name: Tennessee
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Tennessee uses the last four completed quarters only if those do not qualify.
notModeled: The weeks rise above 12, to as many as 20, when Tennessee's average unemployment rate is over 5.5%.
The alternate base period: enter whichever four quarters the Department will use.

citation.sourceDocument: Tenn. Code Ann. §50-7-301 as amended by 2021 Pub. Ch. 560 (from Dec. 1, 2023); TDLWD eligibility pages
citation.sourceNote: Pub. Ch. 560 §1 replaces the benefit table: rows of the average wages in the two highest quarters, $26 wide, from "$ 780.01 through $ 806.00 ... $55.00" to "7,150.01 and over ... 325.00". All 242 rows read on 2026-10-19 equal the average over 26 rounded up plus $24 to $4,420, and plus $49 above it, so no rate between $195 and $219 exists. §2: a claimant is not entitled if base-period earnings are "less than forty (40) times" the rate, or earnings outside the high quarter are "less than the lesser of six (6) times ... or nine hundred dollars ($900)"; weeks are "Twelve (12) ... if the state average unemployment rate is at or below five and five-tenths percent", to 20, and the total rounds down. TDLWD: "Eligible claims may receive up to $325 per week" and "a maximum of 12 weeks ... if the state average unemployment rate is at or below 5.5%." One unpaid waiting week.
